create.name: Canmore Theravada Buddhist Community and Monastery
create.bio:
The Canmore Theravada Buddhist Community is a small monastery for Buddhist nuns in Canmore, Alberta. It began as a weekly sitting group, first called the Bow Valley Sangha, started by Sanghamitta (Mary Dumka), a retired psychiatrist who trained as a lay Dhamma teacher. She later offered her house to become a nuns' monastery, set up a registered charity in 2014, and chose not to tie it to any single Theravada lineage. The bhikkhuni Ayya Ahimsa arrived to live there in December 2022, and the monastery now supports its monastics and a few long-term residents.

The wider community is welcome to join in. There are weekly meditation evenings and mornings, each with chanting, silent sitting and a Dhamma reflection, held in the house and on Zoom, drop-in days of silent meditation on two Saturdays a month, one-to-one interviews, and three or four formal retreats a year. Visiting nuns and monks from the forest and other Theravada traditions come to teach, and the weekly talks are shared on its YouTube channel.

courses.title: Weekend Meditation Retreat with Ayya Ahimsa
courses.description: A weekend retreat at the monastery in Canmore led by its resident nun, Ayya Ahimsa. Retreat details and a registration form are linked from the page.

free_resources.title: Weekly Meditation Groups (in person and Zoom)
free_resources.description: Tuesday evening and Friday morning sessions of chanting, about half an hour of silent sitting and a Dhamma reflection with questions. Open to anyone, Buddhist or not, in the house or online.

free_resources.title: Moon Days of Silence
free_resources.description: Drop-in days of silent sitting and walking meditation at the monastery on the second and fourth Saturdays of each month, with no need to register.

free_resources.title: Videos of Weekly Talks
free_resources.description: Short written summaries of each week's Dhamma talk, many based on a discourse from the Pali Canon, with links to the recordings.
